name: Barium petroleum sulfonate
description: Barium petroleum sulfonate (CAS 61790-48-5 ), also sold as barium petroleum sulfonates or referred to in technical literature as sulfonic acids, petroleum, barium salts, is an oil-soluble metallic sulfonate. It is used primarily as a corrosion inhibitor and detergent additive in lubricant and metalworking formulations. Its barium salt structure provides strong film-forming and emulsification performance in hydrocarbon-based systems. In lubricant additive packages, it functions as a detergent-dispersant, neutralizing acidic combustion byproducts and keeping engine and industrial oil systems clean. This ensures long-term equipment reliability. Metalworking fluid formulators use it to protect ferrous metal surfaces during cutting, drawing, and forming operations. Corrosion protection between processing stages is critical for maintaining high-quality manufacturing standards. It is incorporated into rust-preventive oils and protective coatings applied to steel components during storage and transit. This prevents oxidation and surface degradation in harsh environmental conditions. In oilfield applications, it supports water-in-oil emulsion stability in drilling and completion fluids where hydrocarbon compatibility is required. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy industrial chemistry. Barium petroleum sulfonate is supplied as a viscous liquid or semi-solid, typically dissolved in a mineral oil carrier. The Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most industrial buyers. Product specifications are defined by total base number, barium content, and sulfonate equivalent weight.
